nodes.name: Polystyrene spheres synthesis
nodes.procedure: Sodium styrene sulfonate (0.05 g) and sodium bicarbonate (0.125 g) were dissolved in 200 mL DI water, preheated to 80°C, under stirring at 400 rpm. After a homogeneous solution was formed, 25 mL styrene monomers were added under stirring for another 2 hours, followed by addition of potassium persulfate (0.125g) as an initiator to trigger the polymerization reaction. The reaction proceeded for 18 hours to afford a suspension of uniform polystyrene spheres of 250 nm in size.
nodes.source_text: Sodium styrene sulfonate (0.05 g) and sodium bicarbonate (0.125 g) were dissolved in 200 mL DI water... The reaction proceeded for 18 hours to afford a suspension of uniform polystyrene spheres of 250 nm in size.

nodes.name: PS opal assembly on nickel foam
nodes.procedure: The PS spheres were deposited and self-assembled on the skeleton surfaces of the nickel foam by simply dipping the nickel foam into a PS suspension and drying in an oven set at 40°C for 1 hours three times.
nodes.source_text: The PS spheres were deposited and self-assembled on the skeleton surfaces of the nickel foam by simply dipping the nickel foam into a PS suspension and drying in an oven set at 40°C for 1 hours three times.

nodes.name: NiFeMo alloy electrodeposition into PS opal
nodes.procedure: The electrolyte for the electrodeposition of the NiFeMo alloy contained mixed precursors of 0.9 M nickel sulfate hexahydrate (NiSO4·6H2O), 0.1 M ferrous sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO4·7H2O), and molybdenum chloride ([MoCl5]2) of 0.015 M (optimal). The electrolyte also contained boric acid of 40 g L⁻¹ and saccharin of 1 g L⁻¹. The electrodeposition was conducted in a three-electrode system with a power supply of a CHI 6275D electrochemical workstation. The working electrode (PS sphere dipped 2×2 cm² nickel foam) and counter electrode (Pt foil of 1×1 cm²) were separated by 2 cm and Ag/AgCl served as the reference electrode. The electrodeposition proceeded for 1800 s at a constant voltage of -2.0 V (vs. EAg/AgCl).

nodes.name: PS template removal
nodes.procedure: After the electrodeposition, the PS spheres were removed with etching in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at 60°C to leave behind the NiFeMo or NiFe alloy inverse opals on nickel foam.

nodes.name: NiFeMo IOS
aliases: NiFeMo alloy inverse-opals on nickel foam

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show NiFe IOS and NiFeMo IOS with close-packed structure maintained after PS sphere removal, pore size ~250 nm matching PS template size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The close-packed structure was well maintained even after the etching removal of the PS spheres for formation of the IOS (Figure 2b for NiFe IOS@NF and Figures 2c, S2, and S3 for NiFeMo IOS@NF). The pore size of the IOS is around 250 nm, in good agreement with the size of the templating PS spheres.

properties.description: High-magnification image showing porous structure with nanoparticles or clusters on surface

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS spectra confirm Ni, Fe in NiFe IOS (upper panel) and Ni, Fe, Mo in NiFeMo IOS (lower panel); uniform elemental distributions confirmed by EDX mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The constituent elements of the electrodes were detected with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of a scanning electron microscope (SEM-EDX) to be Ni and Fe for NiFe IOS@NF and Ni, Fe, and Mo for NiFeMo IOS@NF as shown in Figure 2d as the upper and lower panels, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES quantifies NiFe IOS composition as 34% Fe, 66% Ni and NiFeMo IOS as 29% Fe, 69% Ni, 2% Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further quantify the composition of the NiFe IOS and NiFeMo IOS, the NiFe IOS and NiFeMo IOS were scratched off from the skeleton of the nickel foam for inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) measurements.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows fcc Ni phase with (111), (200), (220) peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.4° for both NiFe IOS@NF and NiFeMo IOS@NF; (111) peak shifts to lower angles (44.3° for NiFe, 44.1° for NiFeMo) indicating alloying.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns, shown in Figure 2e, exhibit three pronounced diffraction peaks at 2θ of around 44.5, 51.8, and 76.4°, which can be indexed to the (111), (200), and (220) crystalline planes of fcc Ni phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of NiFeMo IOS shows lattice fringes of 0.208 nm (111) and 0.13 nm (220) planes at 35° angle, slightly larger than pure Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two interlayer distances of 0.208 and 0.13 nm are determined from the zoom-in image, which can be attributed to the crystalline planes of (111) and (220), respectively.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with particle sizes around 100 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDX mapping of NiFeMo IOS shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Mo preserving IOS shape, with intensities matching molar composition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distributions of the constituent elements were examined with elemental energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of a transmission electron microscope (TEM-EDX) mapping shown in Figure 3b.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo6+ peaks at 231.8 eV (3d5/2) and 235.6 eV (3d3/2) in NiFeMo IOS; increased Ni3+ and Fe3+ intensities upon Mo incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the NiFe IOS, no binding energy peaks can be observed for Mo 3d, whereas binding energy peaks located at 231.8 and 235.6 eV emerge for Mo 3d5/2 and Mo 3d3/2 of Mo6+, respectively for the NiFeMo IOS.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates used to determine double layer capacitance Cdl for ECSA calculation; NiFeMo IOS@NF shows ECSA of 98 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S10 shows the current density difference vs. scan rate curves and consequent double layer capacitances of NiFeMo IOS@NF, NiFeMo@NF, NiFe IOS@NF, and NiFe@NF.
